Upstream commit is unverified against the staged tree, and the dependency closure, save/state behaviour, performance and device qualification are all unproven. The adapter HAS now been executed on an AYN Thor (2026-08-09): a LUCENT_INCLUDE_PHASE3_CEMU=1 build routes Wii U INTERNALLY, the adapter reports dual_screen=true, and Cemu brings up both swapchains -- the TV on the primary surface and the GamePad/DRC on the Thor's display 4 (a 1240x1080 secondary surface) -- with Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker HD booting to its title and name-entry screens. It is therefore no longer compile-and-link verified only; what remains unproven for the renderer gate is sustained in-game behaviour and a captured frame in which the DRC scan buffer differs from the TV one. Licence IS cleared (Cemu is MPL-2.0 with no Exhibit B notice, which MPL-2.0 section 3.3 permits distributing under GPL-3.0), but the licence gate stays closed until the dependency closure is pinned.
engines.note: Repository and commit corrected. The previous pin, cemu-project/Cemu at daacdda0bab55dd78a2b5aac2c12d6ebe8c8e868, named the DESKTOP repository and described no artifact: the tree that was actually compiled for the arm64-v8a Lucent native adapter is the Android port (SSimco/Cemu release 0.5), which carries src/android, src/gui/androidgui and src/input/api/Android that the desktop repository does not have. The commit above is the one upstream tag 0.5 points to; the locally staged tree has no .git directory, so it has NOT been verified byte-for-byte against that commit and the source gate stays closed for exactly that reason. An arm64-v8a adapter IS now built and staged at engines/build/arm64-v8a/liblucent_native_adapter_cemu.so, exporting lucent_native_adapter_entry with dual_screen=true, audio wired to Lucent's sink and input wired to the emulated VPAD. Exactly one build of this tree exists, so engines/cemu-source-lock.json records reproducible=false, every gate below stays closed, and shipped stays false. CORRECTION (2026-08-09): an earlier version of this note claimed 'unified-android/build.sh has no Cemu opt-in flag and engines/phase3-qualification-opt-in.json does not list cemu, so Wii U keeps its external route'. BOTH halves were false and the claim caused Wii U to be reported as externally routed when it is not. build.sh DOES read LUCENT_INCLUDE_PHASE3_CEMU (it validates it, requires the staged adapter, bundles the .so, copies the source lock, and re-verifies the packaged bytes against engines/cemu-source-lock.json), and phase3-qualification-opt-in.json DOES list cemu with libraryRouteSystems=[wiiu]. A build made WITH that flag routes Wii U internally; a build made WITHOUT it packages no cemu adapter, NativeAdapterCatalog fails closed, and only then does Wii U fall back to its external route. Omitting the flag is therefore a silent regression, not the default design.
